answers.answer: At London Season, roll one die simultaneously for each held office card, adding one per fatigue and one more for the Chairman. Modified 1–2: no effect; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire the holder to Pensioners, flip the office card to Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not make this normal attrition roll.

Only players who retired at least one pensioner select or discard a displayed card. They act in descending actual total retirement spending; ties go to most total windows including new prizes, then clockwise from the PM. The actor may peek at display blackmails. Do not replace cards while selecting; if the display empties, skip all remaining eligible players. After selection, discard every remaining display card and refill exactly three (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown), even if nobody selected one. Return all unused pensioners to supply.

At phase start check whether your opportunity marker already matches your chosen main action: that action may then be taken twice; otherwise take it once. Move the marker onto the chosen main action. Afterward only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action, which is never doubled and does not move the marker. With four vacant offices, a Writer action places one additional writer once that turn; if the marker matched Writer, two normal placements plus that one bonus place three writers total.

After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one; repeat while both remain. If Debt is gone, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible in order. Court pieces are Company shares. The queue payment was made from family cash to the bank when Seeking a Share, not to Company treasuries.

Fill vacant offices in ascending number on their card backs. The designated hirer chooses and moves a candidate into the office; that family gets the office card. For an ordinary own-family hire, every other player represented in that office's candidate pool must verbally consent. Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt from Nepotism. On promotion, move the old officeholder's fatigue onto the new office card and put the old card vacant in ascending hiring order. If no candidate exists or the hirer is vacant, skip that office; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

Shareholders elect: the former Chairman first announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority (more than half of current shares). Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate backed by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of the winner's shares from Court to the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. If nobody gets the required backing, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself; this fallback is exempt from Nepotism. The Chairman piece still counts as a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in a firm.

For a Company-office check, first commit resources and any cash; all check cash comes from that acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties and roll, using the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and can be retried if resources and office limits permit; 5–6 is catastrophic, ends that office's actions, returns its holder to supply, discards fatigue and flips its card to Vacant Offices. Specific Commander/firm rules may modify this. Do not take an action with no possible effect or success chance, such as trading without a ship or deploying with no dice just to risk officer losses.

The Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, each adding £5 to Balance. Each additional advance needs consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, counting the Chairman, and Debt may never pass the end of its track. The Chairman must then allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved within those limits; cash already in office treasuries stays there for those offices to use.

Shipping must spend its treasury until £2 or less remains. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without its owner's consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China if created. Extra ships last only until Refresh.

The President declares the home region and only regions reachable through open orders within available ship capacity. Each £1 from that President's treasury buys one die; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. A successful check fills at most one order per ship in that Presidency's sea zone, starting with the home-port writer; later orders must extend the connected route made during this Trade. Writers from another Presidency cannot extend it, but writers do not cap capacity: use available writers and then filled-order tokens for remaining ships. Never fill another President's home region, even if that office is vacant. Company Balance gets each order's printed value, halved rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn; President gets £1 per order from the bank and writer owners £1 per placed writer. At most one successful Trade per President per turn; failed tries/retries remain that President's uninterrupted opportunity.

A Commander may target its Presidency's home, an associated region, or a region bordering an associated region, but not another home or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. A Company target must have unrest or a closed order. Exhaust selected officers/regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed dice; subtract the target's strength plus every other region in its empire (count target once; Company defense is zero). On each attempt, afterward, roll one die for every officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 removes that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll for officer losses. Noncatastrophic failure can be retried with remaining resources.

On success, take loot from the bank equal to £4 per target tower plus any faceup loot modifier, with a minimum equal to surviving participating officers plus one for the Commander. Distribute repeatedly: Commander first gets £1 for themself plus £1 per used surviving officer; other families clockwise get £1 per used surviving officer; bank last gets £1 per used regiment and per local-alliance piece, regardless of strength. Repeat cycles until loot is gone. Commander takes one trophy per target tower. Then remove target tower and dome (if capital, remove every matching empire flag in India); open all target orders and clear unrest; on new conquest turn the loot/control token region-symbol side up above the associated President's box, put Governor overlay in the conquered map region and only the Governor card in Vacant Offices. Move Elephant fully inside if it faced outward. A catastrophe returns the Commander and half their family's trophies rounded up, and exhausted officers still check losses; the Commander has no office card to vacate.

Governor starts with its printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces the pool by one regardless of result. On success take £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, and choose exactly one: one stage of Company ship building, one regiment in the President-associated Army, or an unsplit £2 added to Company Balance or that President's treasury. Ship building takes two successful builds total: first puts a partial ship in the Governor's region; next completes it into the President's sea zone. Each Tax after the first this turn adds regional unrest. Any unsuccessful roll adds one unrest; catastrophe also removes the officeholder. Continue with the shrinking pool until stopping, no dice, or catastrophe.

Company expenses reduce Balance by £1 per Debt, each officer/regiment in an Army, and each ship in a sea zone (including China), excluding Commanders. If cash is short, take £5 emergency loans; each advances Debt only while a track space remains. At maximum Debt, keep taking loans without advancing Debt. New emergency Debt adds no expense this turn; after the loans set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations at current Standing and lower Standing one if below them. Then the Chairman may pay affordable dividends at one cash per share, paying each owner £1 per share including themself; if total dividends strictly exceed expectations, Standing rises one.
answers.evidence: Revenue — Company expenses, expectations and dividends (lines 159–167)

answers.answer: A primary Crisis against a Company region is resolved first, then secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest, in Bombay–Madras–Bengal Army order; each Commander chooses the order within that Presidency. Primary normal Crisis strength is its normal Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in its target. Primary Foreign Invasion uses only its ordinary attack die; each secondary Rebellion uses only that region's unrest cubes. Associated Commander exhausts active Army pieces equal to the Crisis strength, or as many as possible; local alliances are usable once and cannot be split between purposes. If newly exhausted strength equals the attack, defense succeeds: remove all target unrest, award Commander one trophy, and if it defeated a normal primary Invasion also remove one attacker tower if possible. If unequal, attack succeeds and Region Loss follows. The summary leaves the counting of an indivisible alliance's excess strength unresolved (specifically strength 2 versus attack 1), so that edge case is uncertain.
answers.evidence: Events in India — Attacks on Company and Mounting defense (lines 193–208); FAQ source gap (line 439)

answers.answer: A vote at support −1 or lower fails: discard the law, resolve a dilemma's If Failed text, and Opposition Leader returns the token and takes the PM dial; the new PM moves the proposed policy one adjacent space either way and resolves that adjacent policy. Support zero or higher passes: put the law with passed laws, PM takes a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy, then immediate law effects. Restore all used voting cards to normal orientation after either result. If a law causes Company failure, finish the vote before scoring.

In 1758 and Long 1710, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call a special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. Use ordinary voting and support threshold, except there is no policy; failure neither removes PM nor discards the Deregulation law, and PM may vote against. Passing lowers Debt one per two current Debt, sets Standing to S, gives PM a passed-law token and activates firms. Failure increases Company-share scoring value by flipping/placing the Court VP token, up to ±3. 1813 starts deregulated; 1710 has no deregulation procedure. No usual policy accompanies the vote.

To form a firm, a player managing none contributes one eligible Company share (return it to supply) or flips a workshop to invested; flip family board to firm charter, place a member as first share, set value cube to leftmost space and take £5 from bank into London treasury. With manager consent, further Company-share/workshop contributions create a share and add £5 from bank to London; maximum ten shares, but investments beyond ten still add £5 without a share. Cannot use Chairman share, any shares when Standing or Debt is on a lined space, or shares created this turn (even if traded away). Invested workshops never revert, lose bonus and failure VP, and stay invested even if firm fails. Firm money is distinct from family cash.
answers.evidence: Deregulation — firm treasury rules and investments (lines 347, 351–357)

answers.answer: Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn and needs at least one ship to choose trade; it may choose a closed home port, but the home port must be open when filled. Managers secretly select zone/home port and cash bid, or Hobnob, then reveal bids simultaneously while strategies stay facedown until the matching Presidency. At that Presidency's start, firms reveal and roll one die per £1 bid, paying bid to bank; at least one 1/2 permits trade. Initiative is ships minus successful dice. President's successful Trade also sets initiative; after it, fill lowest initiative first, President choosing ties (Company does not automatically go first). If President is vacant or never succeeds, firms fill after Commander/Governors, with Chairman breaking initiative ties. Fill open orders along each firm's own route from home, up to ships +1; each firm cannot refill its own order but may refill another firm's or Company's order, and Company may refill firm orders. Previously filled orders yield half listed revenue rounded down. Revenue goes to India treasury; advance Value one space per full £6 added there this turn.
answers.evidence: Firms — Firm strategies and competing trade (lines 362–375)

answers.answer: At start of Revenue before Company, firms pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or firm Value, using London and/or India treasury. If unable, dissolve unless rescued. Dissolution sends shares to Debtor's Prison (−1 VP each), ships to matching shipyards, charter to family side; invested workshops remain invested. Rescue can use emergency investments under normal Company-share/workshop restrictions (even at ten shares, cash still comes in but no new share; Value drops one per emergency investment and remaining cash is lost), or a one-firm emergency merger with all involved shareholders consenting. After expenses, dividends may be paid only from India: each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 manager. A shareholder may waive any number of shares only with manager consent. Record total actual cash paid, not per-share amount, as dividend marker; active non-Hobnob firm with no payout records zero, Hobnob retains prior marker. Sweep remaining India money to London.

Supplies of components are limited; when one runs out, do as much as possible. Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. All information is public, including discards and family cash, except facedown blackmail and firm strategies/bids concealed temporarily during selection.

Negotiations may transfer enterprises, facedown blackmail, family treasury cash, Company/firm shares and promise cards. They may not transfer officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, PM dial or Chairman piece. To transfer a share, return the old owner's family member and replace it at that location with a piece from the receiving family; adjust VP if luxury ownership changes. Blackmail must remain facedown when traded; played faceup blackmail cannot be traded.

Immediate transfers are binding; promises of future behavior are not, except a printed promise card's guaranteed effect can be called if possible and within its timing/limits. No promise calls during Final Scoring. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, guarantor chooses which to fulfill. Promise cards may be transferred to a third party or back to guarantor. A transferred resource cannot activate twice (for example, a workshop already paying this Bonuses phase does not pay again after sale in that phase).

Use the scenario's player setup cards; add three extra cards for five players or six extra for six, shuffle and deal evenly. Each player takes the listed cash, enterprises and positions, placing holdings per the table; an office includes its family member and matching office card. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Shuffle prestige and blackmail together into one deck; deal three for London display, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown. Shuffle remaining laws.

The game ends after the scenario's final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Failure during Events in India means finish that phase before Final Scoring; failure caused by legislation means finish the vote first. Once game over, stop negotiations, promise calls and playing blackmail unless a card explicitly permits final-scoring use; no negotiations or promise calls are allowed during Final Scoring.

Final Power counts enterprises and Company shares at their current Power-track rates (bottom two positions score zero), plus one per passed-law token and trophy, two for PM, and applicable printed card power including blackmail and spouse. Highest and second awards are 3/1 VP on final turns 1–3, 5/2 on turns 4–6, and 8/4 on turns 7–8. If tied for first, each tied player gets only the lower award and nobody else scores; tied second receive nothing. Highest final VP wins; ties go to most windows, then clockwise from PM.
answers.evidence: Scoring — Power award and victory ties (lines 399, 412)

answers.answer: If Company survived, add current Court VP value per Company share; if failed, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop (scores may be negative). Survived Company outcome then rolls office attrition and retires Pensioners without prestige cards. Failed outcome instead draws one random Company failure card. In either outcome, if deregulated, firm scoring and the eligible firm special retirement occur earlier in Final Scoring; that retirement is not replaced by the failure card.
answers.evidence: Scoring — Final Scoring order, Court/workshops and outcomes (lines 389–408)

answers.answer: Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred; required enterprise/share trades happen immediately when taking one. Retirement discounts are personal, can stack, and each is usable once per London Season and once during Final Scoring. Discounts reduce actual spending (and thus prestige-card priority). Specific spouse effects remain on the spouse card.
answers.evidence: London Season — Spouses and discounts (line 94); source boundary (line 435)

answers.answer: If a shipyard is returned because of Violet Effingham or unpaid tax, its fitted ship remains in play. That yard cannot be purchased while its matching ship remains in play; it becomes available after the ship returns.

Enlist Writer: no listed cost; place a member in any Presidency Writers box, plus one additional writer once this turn if at least four offices are vacant. Enlist Officer: no listed cost; place a member in Officers-in-Training. Purchase Luxury: pay £4 to bank; gain luxury, 2 VP while owned and a window icon (social enterprise). Purchase Shipyard: pay £2 to bank; take yard and put matching ship unfitted on it (shipping enterprise, one vote and £1 bonus while fitted). Purchase Workshop: pay £5 to bank; gain manufacturing enterprise, two votes, £1 bonus, and worth 1 VP on Company failure if uninvested. Seek Share: place member on empty queue space and pay £2, £3, £3, £4 or £5 to bank; it is only an applicant until later issuance.

If a required family piece is unavailable in supply, take one from any of your prizes and lose that prize's printed VP. This also applies to creating a firm share. If no Family action is possible, take none and return your opportunity marker to supply.

If Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns as Chairman, placing a family member from supply, or if necessary a prize member (losing that prize's VP), if possible. If neither source can provide a piece, there is no Chairman. This is the empty-Court automatic rule, not the shareholder campaign/fallback election.

Chairman is elected by shareholders. Chairman hires Director of Trade from current officeholders other than Chairman/Governor, or any writer if all offices are vacant; Manager of Shipping from any writer; Military Affairs from a Presidential Commander, else any officer, else any trainee. Director hires a President from a writer of that Presidency or a Governor associated with it. Associated President hires a Governor from a writer or officer in the region (not its Commander). Chairman hires China Superintendent from any writer immediately when China is created. Governor General replaces Director and is hired the same way as Director. A vacant hirer means skip the office; candidates/fallbacks are limited as listed.
answers.evidence: Hiring — Office and candidate table (lines 134–143); Hiring vacancy rule (line 122)

answers.answer: Director may make repeated Special Envoy checks, spending £1 of its treasury per die and taking no penalty. Each success either opens one closed order in a non-Company region or opens China (place Superintendent overlay/card and Chairman immediately hires a writer). After all envoys, Director may transfer up to two pieces total, each one writer or ship between any Presidencies/sea zones, including China after creation. Transfers cannot happen while Envoys are still being taken.

Military Affairs may first make up to two transfers, each one officer or regiment from one Army to another, keeping it in the top half. Then assign every Officer-in-Training to any Army's top half. Finally appoint Commanders: if a slot is vacant or a different family has more total pieces in that Army than the incumbent's family, choose among families with the most pieces; move a chosen officer to Commander slot and return previous Commander to top half as officer. A tie with incumbent's family does not replace them. Nepotism does not apply.

Each President chooses the order of its Commander, Governors and Trade; Commander/Governors must be given an opportunity but may decline. Each position finishes all actions before the next begins; Trade can be before or after those positions but cannot interrupt one. If a President is vacant, Chairman sets the order only and cannot Trade or approve local-alliance purchases.

Trade does not exhaust ships. On a nonfinal Refresh, return writers from orders to their associated Presidency's Writers box, using dividers to preserve affiliation; return filled tokens and dividers to supply. The Presidency-specific affiliation matters even if writers are adjacent on the map.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations and Trade (line 268); Upkeep and Refresh (lines 229–240)

answers.answer: At the start of Commander operations, before Deploy, request the President's treasury money for printed-price local alliances in the Army; President must approve. Move purchased alliances to top/active. Using one for Deploy or defense exhausts the whole alliance to bottom; its full printed strength is usable once that turn and cannot be split among purposes. Refresh also exhausts any unused active alliances; it never reactivates them, unlike officers/regiments. Exact counting of an alliance's excess defense strength is explicitly unresolved by the summary.
answers.evidence: Actions — Commanders and Deploy (line 272); Events in India — defense source gap (lines 199–208, 439)

answers.answer: For a Deploy into one's own Company region to reopen orders or clear unrest, Company defense penalty is zero. It has no tower, so it gives zero tower trophies. With no tower and no faceup loot modifier, take minimum loot equal to surviving participating officers plus £1 for the Commander and distribute it normally.

Each successful Build is one stage: if no partial ship is in the Governor's region, that success places it there; if one is already there, a success completes it into the sea zone associated with that Governor's President. Thus two successes total. A commissioned regiment goes into the Army associated with that President; it has officer-like strength, its loot is paid to bank, and it does not cause officer-loss rolls.

Successful Special Envoy can open China, placing Superintendent overlay/card and having Chairman immediately hire any writer; Envoy to China law also creates it and immediately hires a writer. Its treasury holds ships, not cash. Shipping and Director may send ships there as to a sea zone. It acts after Bengal. China ships count as Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws.
answers.evidence: Actions — Director of Trade (line 252); Superintendent of Trade in China (line 326)

answers.answer: China gets one trade attempt after Bengal, including failed attempts, so no retry. Without an export icon in Company-controlled regions, do not attempt it. Roll one die per ship. On success count export icons only in Company-controlled regions: Company Balance gets £4 per icon and Superintendent's family gets £1 per icon from bank. Non-Company export icons count for neither payment.

When Governor General law creates the office, make all Governors pensioners, remove their overlays and partial Company ships, and return Governor/Director cards to the box. Replace Director with Governor General preserving holder and fatigue and place ribbon overlay. Later conquests create no Governor or overlay; printed Company symbols show control. On region loss, skip Governor elimination. Governor General hires Presidents and uses Director's former treasury/turn position; it is hired like Director and rolls attrition normally.

Before any Govern check, add £3 to Balance per Company region. Govern attempts cost £1 per die from its treasury, no penalty; on every rolled six, add one unrest to each Company region, even on success. Failure adds one more unrest to every Company region. On success, gain £1 per Company region and choose one benefit for each: complete a Company ship into any sea zone including China; add a regiment to any Army; or add £2 to Balance or any office treasury except its own, placing unrest in a Company region. Multiple Tax choices this turn must place unrest in different regions. At most one successful Govern per turn.

Storm die first identifies affected zones. For each player-owned ship in those zones, roll once: 1–2 no effect; 3–4 add fatigue, or sink it if already fatigued; 5–6 sink it. Sunk ships return unfatigued to matching shipyards. Company and extra ships are exempt. China counts as Eastern. Firm ships use their chosen strategy zone; Hobnob ships are exempt from storms.
answers.evidence: Events in India — Storms (lines 171–173); Firms trade (line 383)

answers.answer: When an order closes, return any writer on it to its owner's supply; flip a filled token to closed. If instructed to close an order in an already fully closed region, Cascade: close all open orders directly connected to orders in that region. If a connected order is already closed, close that connected region's northernmost open order instead; if none are open, it also Cascades. A region can initiate a Cascade only once per event tile but can receive effects from multiple Cascades.
answers.evidence: Events in India — Closing orders and Cascades (line 175)

answers.answer: Turmoil closes the northernmost open order in the region shown by the back of the new top draw-stack tile; if all are closed, Cascade. Windfall pays owners £1 per writer on orders in that top-stack region and every bordering region. Shuffle first moves Elephant, then shuffles that event tile into the remaining draw stack and separately shuffles discards onto the top. If the draw stack is empty, March last instead.

Leader looks at the back of the new top tile: a sovereign region gains one tower; a dominated region instead rebels with the printed explosion modifier. March Elephant only if it was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.

Peace on an Elephant border opens orders connected across the border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region. If Elephant is fully inside a region, open all its orders and remove its unrest instead. Then March in either case.

For an ordinary Invasion, compare the attacker's whole empire strength plus event modifier to defender's whole empire strength; attacker must be strictly greater, so a tie fails. On success replace defender's flag with attacker's dominated flag; taking a capital shatters its whole empire. If attacker had no empire, use a free capital/star flag and matching small flag; if none are available, no new empire/flags form. On failure attacker loses one tower. The summary does not supply a separate rule for a non-Company Invasion with missing flags beyond that availability rule.

For a non-Company Rebellion, compare only the rebelling region's strength plus modifier to its sovereign capital's strength; other regions of the empire do not count. The rebel must be strictly greater, so equality fails. On success the actor becomes sovereign, its flag is removed and all its orders close (Cascade if already closed). On failure, remove one tower from the capital.

On Region Loss, Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up and the Commander member goes to supply. Roll once per officer in associated Army; each 6 removes that officer. Eliminate Governor: card to unused stack, fatigue/member to supplies, overlay removed; also remove partial Company ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion's specified strength) and appropriate invasion flag. Return control token to its region with £ loot side down and region-symbol side up; future conquest gets no loot modifier and region loses Presidency association. Close all orders for an Invasion Crisis (Cascade if already closed); Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing loss accumulates by regions lost so far this turn: first −1, second additional −2, etc. Other Company regions are not lost automatically; resolve their attacks/defenses separately.

After successful Invasion Crisis, Elephant moves to the successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); after other Marches it goes to the region on the back of the new top stack tile. If destination is Company-controlled, place Elephant fully inside; if dominated, point it toward its sovereign; if sovereign, point across the shape-marked border on that tile. If that neighbor is already dominated by the actor, choose first clockwise neighbor not dominated; if all are dominated, use redirect-arrow shape border pointing toward empire capital.

Foreign Invasion uses storm die to choose target Presidencies: West targets Bombay, South Madras, East Bengal, all storms means each, none means the top-stack region. For each target roll an ordinary die for attack strength and resolve Invasion/Company attack. Unrest does not add to primary attack strength or determine towers. On success close all target orders (Cascade if already all closed), remove its flag and all matching flags if it is a capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, and set tower strength to half the attack roll rounded down. March with circle shape only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded.
answers.evidence: Events in India — Foreign Invasion and ruling (lines 185, 443)

answers.answer: PM draws at least one law, revealing one at a time. After one or two ordinary (non-dilemma) draws, PM may stop or continue up to three total; choose one revealed law and discard the others. Drawing a dilemma forces selection of that dilemma and immediately ends drawing. Before voting, PM moves dial clockwise or counterclockwise to the first policy space matching the chosen law's bottom icon; that space sets target and consequence. Read law and set Vote marker to its printed starting support.

Tax makes each family pay £1 to bank per target it owns; unpaid targets return to supply, including Chairman if taxed. Window tax additionally charges each window on enterprises and each family member's prize; return unpaid enterprise/member. Bonus means bank pays each family £1 per target it owns. Power swaps target marker with next higher Power marker; if already highest, swap any other pair.

Each £1 of family cash buys one vote, plus printed card votes. A card's votes can be used only once during the entire vote, across all rounds; rotate it when used and leave rotated until resolution. PM starts each clockwise round and may call another full round or stop after each; a round with no votes ends voting. Tracks have no limits. Restore used cards at resolution.

A player who voted for may later oppose, but once opposed cannot vote for in that vote. Track opposition; the biggest opponent is Opposition Leader, with tied current holder retaining the role. With recipient's consent, votes can be cast for someone already opposed or committing to oppose and add to that person's opposition total. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except forced use of the 'Vote with my enterprises' promise.

Yes. On the final turn pay upkeep normally, then skip Refresh and go to Final Scoring. Pay printed upkeep separately for each family member on a prize; if unpaid return that member and lose its printed VP. On nonfinal Refresh, writers on orders return to their associated Presidency Writers box; filled tokens and Presidency dividers return to supply; extra ships return to supply; exhausted Army officers and regiments reactivate; active local alliances exhaust and do not reactivate; fitted player ships keep fatigue. Then advance turn and begin London Season.

In a London Season, each shareholder may make one extra retirement from supply rather than Pensioners, regardless of how many firms they own. Actual cash spent after spouse discounts cannot exceed the highest total dividend marker of any firm they have a share in. No retirement from a firm with absent or zero marker. Discounts may permit a prize whose printed cost exceeds the marker; other retirement rules apply, including prestige eligibility. At start of Final Scoring, score firms, then allow one special retirement regardless of Company success/failure, before Power or ordinary scoring and with no display cards.
answers.evidence: Deregulation — Special retirement (line 349); Final Scoring order (lines 389–395)

answers.answer: Investment cash is paid by bank into London treasury; trade revenue goes to India treasury. London pays ship fitting and trade bids; firm expenses may use either/both treasuries; dividends come only from India. Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries; money moves only through specified investment, payout and expense rules.
answers.evidence: Deregulation — Firm treasuries (line 347); firms (lines 357, 371, 379, 383); Cash location (line 433)

answers.answer: Firms phase follows Family share creation and precedes Hiring. Investments occur without set order until nobody wants more; firm manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm and PM resolves conflicts between firms. Then managers choose strategies.

Manager may fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 from firm's London treasury to bank, with yard owner's consent. A firm cannot acquire Company or extra ships. It may buy a player-owned ship already in Company with owner consent: pay £3 if unfatigued or £2 if fatigued into Shipping treasury. The summary's purchase permission is for a player-owned ship already in Company; it does not say purchase is limited to fitted shipyards beyond that description.

Only a player who manages no firm at all may initiate hostile takeover. Get consent of holders of a majority of target firm's shares. Move target's ships, money and shares to the initiating player's charter and copy both cube positions; former manager returns cubes and flips board to family side. Managing another firm also disqualifies the initiator.

Managers negotiate and every shareholder must consent. Highest-value firm is primary; if tied, players choose among tied firms. Transfer all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family sides. Share transfers may be negotiated. If primary would exceed ten shares, return excess shares to their owners' supplies with those owners' consent. The whole agreement is one binding immediate transfer; primary's value/dividend tracks continue.
Hobnob has no bid, trade or dividends; the firm still pays expenses and keeps its previous dividend marker for retirement. Its ships are exempt from storms.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies and competing trade (lines 364–370); expenses and dividends (lines 379–383)

answers.answer: Yes. Emergency investment follows normal Company-share/workshop rules; even when the ten-share cap prevents another share, investment adds £5 from bank to London. Each emergency investment lowers firm Value one space, including if no share can be created; pay expenses, then lose any remaining cash. Other restrictions persist, including not using Company shares created this turn, even if traded away.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends (line 381); Investments (line 356)

answers.answer: Emergency negotiated merger may involve only one other firm. Normal merger rules still apply, including consent from every shareholder involved. The other firm must first pay its own expenses if it has not already, then cover the endangered firm's unpaid expenses.

Voluntary dissolution requires consent of all shareholders. Use the insolvent-firm dissolution procedure: shares go to Debtor's Prison (−1 VP each), ships return to matching shipyards, and charter flips to family side. Invested workshops stay invested for the rest of the game and do not recover.

In Final Scoring, if deregulated first calculate each player's VP from all their shares across all firms, then round that player's total down once; deduct 1 VP per own family piece in Debtor's Prison. Value 1–10 share rates are −1, 0, ½, ½, 1, 1, 1, 1½, 1½, 2 respectively. This firm scoring occurs before firm special retirement, Power, ordinary Court/workshops and survival/failure outcome, and still occurs if Company failed.
Prize levels per family member are: cost £2, upkeep £0, 0 VP, 0 windows; £4, £1, 2 VP, 1 window; £8, £2, 4 VP, 2 windows; £14, £3, 8 VP, 3 windows; £20, £4, 12 VP, 4 windows.

1710 is turns 1–5 and has no deregulation procedures. 1758 is turns 3–7 and may vote in deregulation. 1813 is turns 5–8 and starts deregulated. Long 1710 is turns 1–8, same initial position as 1710 with deregulation available separately; it may take eight turns and can run about twice as long.

1710: Standing expectations £10, Debt 0, each office treasury £3, Royal Protection law, one regiment per Army and no Company ships. 1758: Standing £12, Debt 3, each office treasury £4, Calico Acts, one regiment per Army, one Company ship in East Indian, and Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency. The listed initial laws are setup laws, not passed-law tokens.

1813 starts at Standing expectations £10 and Debt 0, with £3 in each office treasury; initial laws Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor's Prison side) and Calico Acts; two regiments per Army and one Company ship per sea zone. Put +2/−2 share-value token in Court, create China, put Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in their Presidencies, return Governor General law to box and place its overlay over Director of Trade; use Governor General instead of Director and no Governors. Copy map details from scenario-card reverse. Starting player offices/ships also depend on dealt setup cards.

Final-turn Power award for first/second is 3/1 VP on turns 1–3, 5/2 on turns 4–6, and 8/4 on turns 7–8. If first is tied, every tied player gets only the lower award for that turn band (1, 2 or 4 VP), and no second award is given to others.

Initial Power positions: Social 2, Company shares 1, Shipping 0, Manufacturing 0. In 1758/Long 1710, special vote at start of turn before London Season is optional if Standing and/or Debt is lined and mandatory if either is starred. Lined Standing: £4/£6/£8; lined Debt: 5/6/7/8; starred: Standing £4 and Debt 8. Standing reset space S is above £10.

No. The designer ruling says unrest does not add to Foreign Invasion's primary attack or determine resulting tower level. Use the ordinary attack die for both attack strength and halving to set towers. On success close every target order once; if already all closed, Cascade. Region Loss does not close them again.

Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reducing a check to zero dice means failure. Company Fraud occurs at start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice the highest roll (minimum zero), and take bank cash only equal to the actual Balance reduction, so do not pay more than Balance removed. Public Demands Impeachment returns the member to supply and office card to Vacant Offices. Military Oversight's demoted Commander is eligible as an officer for reappointment. These are card-specific effects.

answers.answer: Set board and supplies; shuffle India events; put local alliances in their named Army boxes; set Company Balance to £5, starting Power positions as indicated and family VP markers to zero; put loot tokens money-side up in matching regions. Choose a scenario and follow its setup card for Standing, Debt, treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and India political map; put Turn marker on its listed date and PM dial arm on that matching date. Scenario determines final turn. Player setup cards then give additional holdings/positions; scenario card reverse provides exact map where indicated.

Normal order: London Season → Family → Firms (if deregulated) → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh. A special eligible Deregulation vote is at the very start of a turn before London Season. Skip London Season on the game's first turn; Firms phase occurs after Family when deregulated.

Retirements start with Chairman; if vacant, use former Chairman, then proceed clockwise. Each player may retire each pensioner to a prize, paying its printed cost and moving member to prize for printed VP; spending is held aside until London Season ends to determine display selection order, then paid to bank. Pensioners need not be retired, but any unused pensioners return to supply after the display step and do not remain for another turn.

No. Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove the surviving capital's starred flag so it is no longer an empire. This applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest.
Per firm share by Value: 1 = −1 VP; 2 = 0; 3 = ½; 4 = ½; 5 = 1; 6 = 1; 7 = 1; 8 = 1½; 9 = 1½; 10 = 2. Each player's total across all firms is rounded down once after summing.

answers.answer: The Chairman title holder takes the first Family action, then players act clockwise. Each resolves the Family action sequence; after all players have acted, New Company Shares are issued: while Debt and applicants remain, move rightmost applicant to Court and lower Debt one, repeating; if no Debt, slide applicants right preserving order.

Follow ribbon order: Chairman → Director of Trade (or Governor General replacing Director) → Manager of Shipping → Military Affairs → Bombay → Madras → Bengal → China Superintendent if created. Skip every vacant office; it remains vacant and takes no action. Office creations generally go to Vacant Offices until hiring, except China gets immediate hire when created.

Events begin by rolling storm die, whose face specifies affected sea zones and number of India events. Resolve all storms before any event draw; storm checks are once per player-owned ship in affected zones, while Company and extra ships are exempt. Then flip and resolve event tiles one at a time from draw stack for the number printed on die face. When an event uses a region, normally use the back of the new top tile, not the tile just drawn, subject to its specific rule.

For an ordinary Elephant-located Crisis, tail is attacker/acting region and head is defender. Sovereign actor (large capital flag or unflagged dome) means Invasion; dominated actor (small flag or no dome) means Rebellion against sovereign. Elephant fully inside a Company region means Rebellion against Company. These map markers distinguish sovereign/dominated status; this classifier is for ordinary Elephant-located Crisis, while Foreign Invasion has its own location rule.
